tests.name: Quick Check
tests.description: Timed check on The Role of Education

questions.question: Compare Functionalist and Marxist views of the role of education.
questions.correctAnswer: Functionalism: education transmits norms (Durkheim), allocates roles by merit (Parsons), provides social mobility. Marxism: education transmits ruling class ideology (Althusser), corresponds to workplace hierarchy (Bowles & Gintis), reproduces class inequality. Key difference: Functionalism sees education serving everyone; Marxism sees it serving the ruling class.

questions.question: Explain what the hidden curriculum is and evaluate its importance in education.
questions.correctAnswer: The hidden curriculum teaches: obedience (follow rules without questioning), hierarchy (teachers have authority over pupils), competition (grades, rankings), punctuality and attendance. Functionalists: this socialises young people for society. Marxists: this produces compliant workers for capitalism. Evaluation: the hidden curriculum exists but its effects vary - some students resist and question

questions.question: Evaluate whether the education system is meritocratic.
questions.correctAnswer: Meritocracy means equal opportunity based on ability and effort. Evidence for: comprehensive schools aim to give all children the same education; exam results are (mostly) blind-marked. questions.question: Full-Mark Response Evaluate the view that the education system serves the interests of the ruling class. <div class="
questions.correctAnswer: A grade 9 response will: present Marxist evidence (Althusser's ISA, Bowles & Gintis' correspondence principle, hidden curriculum, cultural capital); present Functionalist counter-evidence (education provides social solidarity and skills, enables some social mobility); evaluate using evidence on class inequality in achievement (working-class underachievement); conclude: the education system does serve ruling class interests by reproducing class inequality, but it also provides genuine opportunities for some working-class students. The system is not purely ideological - it has dual functions: maintaining inequality AND enabling some social mobility. The question is whether the balance favours reproduction or mobility.
